\chapter{Chapter08 — Decision Tree Exercises}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter08.DecisionTreeExercises
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter08.DecisionTreeExercises}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Coordinatewise disjunction]
\lean{FABL.orOnCoordinates}
\label{FABL.orOnCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
For a finite set of available coordinates among $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, define a Boolean
function on sign vectors $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ that equals $1$ if $x_i=1$ for every available
coordinate $i$, and equals $-1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Empty-coordinate OR function]
\lean{FABL.orOnCoordinates_empty}
\label{FABL.orOnCoordinates_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.orOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$, the function that returns $1$ exactly when all
coordinates in the empty set are $1$ is the constant function with value $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Full-coordinate OR function]
\lean{FABL.orOnCoordinates_univ}
\label{FABL.orOnCoordinates_univ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.orFunction, FABL.orOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$, the function that returns $1$ exactly when all
coordinates in the full set $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$ are $1$ agrees with the function that
returns $1$ exactly when every coordinate is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Sequential OR decision tree construction]
\lean{FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux}
\label{FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.Sign}
For a finite set of available coordinates in $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$, define a decision
tree that queries the least available coordinate. If its value is $-1$, the tree returns
$-1$; otherwise it continues recursively on the remaining coordinates. If no coordinates
are available, it returns $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sequential OR decision tree]
\lean{FABL.sequentialOrTree}
\label{FABL.sequentialOrTree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.Sign, FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux}
For each natural number $n$, define the decision tree on $n$ sign-valued inputs that
queries coordinates in increasing order, returns $-1$ as soon as a queried value is
$-1$, and returns $1$ if every input value is different from $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sequential OR tree correctness]
\lean{FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux_computes}
\label{FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.Computes, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval, FABL.orOnCoordinates, FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A$ be a set of coordinates in $\text{Fin }n$, and
let $x$ assign a sign in $\\{ -1,1 \\}$ to each coordinate. The decision tree that
queries the available coordinates in increasing order, returns $-1$ as soon as it finds
a coordinate with value $-1$, and returns $1$ if all queried coordinates have value $1$
computes the function that is $1$ exactly when every coordinate in $A$ has value $1$,
and is $-1$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sequential OR tree correctness]
\lean{FABL.sequentialOrTree_computes}
\label{FABL.sequentialOrTree_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.Computes, FABL.orFunction, FABL.orOnCoordinates_univ, FABL.sequentialOrTree, FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux_computes}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $x$ assign a sign in $\{ -1,1 \}$ to each of its $n$
coordinates. The decision tree that queries the coordinates in increasing order, returns
$-1$ as soon as it finds a coordinate with value $-1$, and returns $1$ if every
coordinate has value $1$ computes the function that is $1$ exactly when every coordinate
has value $1$, and is $-1$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Average query cost]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount, FABL.productMean}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $T$ be a finite decision tree with outputs in $\alpha$. Its auxiliary average cost
is the product-distribution mean of its query count on inputs whose coordinates are
independently sampled according to $\pi$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of average cost definitions]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_complete}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_complete}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.deterministicAverageCost}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ and $\alpha$ be finite sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, and let $T$ be a finite decision tree on $n$ coordinates with leaves labelled
in $\alpha$. The auxiliary average cost of $T$ under the product distribution with
coordinate law $\pi$ equals its deterministic average cost under that same distribution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of average query cost]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_nonneg}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost, FABL.pmfExpectation_nonneg, FABL.productMean}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ and $\alpha$ be finite sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, and let $T$ be a finite decision tree on $n$ coordinates with leaves labelled
in $\alpha$. Its auxiliary average cost under the product distribution with coordinate
law $\pi$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average cost at a query node]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_query}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_query}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.productMean_diagonal_section, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_eq_of_agreeOn, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add_fun, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.productMean, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ and $\alpha$ be finite sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, and suppose there is a finite Fourier basis for functions on $\Omega$ that is
orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$ and contains the constant-one
function. For an available coordinate $i$ and a family of decision trees $T_v$ indexed
by $v\in\Omega$, with each $T_v$ using only the other available coordinates, the tree
that queries $i$ and then follows $T_{x_i}$ has auxiliary average cost
$1+\mathbb{E}_{v\sim\pi}[\text{auxiliary average cost of }T_v]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average query cost of a sequential OR tree]
\lean{FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux_averageCost}
\label{FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux_averageCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.productMean_diagonal_section, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_eq_of_agreeOn, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.Sign, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.biasedSiteFourierBasis, FABL.orAverageQueryCost, FABL.orAverageQueryCost_succ, FABL.pmfExpectation_add_fun, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.productMean, FABL.replaceCoordinate, FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let
$p\in(0,1)$. On independent signs whose probability of being $-1$ is $p$, the expected
number of queries made by the tree that queries the coordinates of $A$ in increasing
order and stops at the first $-1$ (or after exhausting $A$) is
$\sum_{k=0}^{|A|-1}(1-p)^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average cost of the sequential OR tree]
\lean{FABL.sequentialOrTree_averageCost}
\label{FABL.sequentialOrTree_averageCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_complete, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.deterministicAverageCost, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.orAverageQueryCost, FABL.sequentialOrTree, FABL.sequentialOrTreeAux_averageCost}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p$ satisfy $0<p<1$. For an input of $n$ independent
signs, each equal to $-1$ with probability $p$ and to $1$ with probability $1-p$, the
expected number of coordinate queries made by the sequential OR decision tree is
$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(1-p)^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average cost of computing OR]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.orAverageQueryCost_le_auxiliaryAverageCost}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.orAverageQueryCost_le_auxiliaryAverageCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.Computes, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_nonneg, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_query, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval_eq_of_agreeOn, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.biasedSiteFourierBasis, FABL.orAverageQueryCost, FABL.orAverageQueryCost_succ, FABL.orOnCoordinates, FABL.pmfExpectation_biasedSignPMF, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.productMean, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<p<1$, and let $A$ be a set of coordinates in
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. If a decision tree with sign-valued queries and sign-valued outputs
computes the function that returns $1$ exactly when every coordinate in $A$ has value
$1$, then its expected number of queries under the product distribution of independent
signs with probability $p$ of being $-1$ is at least $\sum_{k=0}^{|A|-1}(1-p)^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average Query Cost for Sign OR]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.orAverageQueryCost_le_averageCost}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.orAverageQueryCost_le_averageCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.auxiliaryAverageCost_complete, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.orAverageQueryCost_le_auxiliaryAverageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.deterministicAverageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.exists_deterministic_averageCost_le, FABL.Sign, FABL.biasedSignPMF, FABL.orAverageQueryCost, FABL.orFunction, FABL.orOnCoordinates_univ}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<p<1$, and let $T$ be a zero-error randomized
decision tree computing the function that returns $1$ exactly when all $n$ input signs
are $1$ and returns $-1$ otherwise. If the input coordinates are sampled independently,
with each sign equal to $-1$ with probability $p$ and $1$ with probability $1-p$, then
$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(1-p)^k$ is at most the average query cost of $T$ under this input
distribution.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b001}
For every natural number $n$ and every real $p$ with $0<p<1$, the minimum average query
cost of a zero-error randomized decision tree computing the OR function on $n$
independent signs, each equal to $1$ with probability $1-p$, is
$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(1-p)^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Critical probability for the OR function]
\lean{FABL.orCriticalProbability}
\label{FABL.orCriticalProbability}
\leanok
For each natural number $n$, define $p_c=1-\exp\!\left(-\frac{\log 2}{n}\right)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Power at the OR critical probability]
\lean{FABL.one_sub_orCriticalProbability_pow}
\label{FABL.one_sub_orCriticalProbability_pow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.orCriticalProbability}
\difficulty{3}
For a positive natural number $n$, let $p=1-\exp(-\log(2)/n)$. Then $(1-p)^n=\tfrac12$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the critical probability]
\lean{FABL.orCriticalProbability_pos}
\label{FABL.orCriticalProbability_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.orCriticalProbability}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n>0$, the critical probability $1-\exp(-\log(2)/n)$ is
positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds on the critical probability]
\lean{FABL.orCriticalProbability_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.orCriticalProbability_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.orCriticalProbability, FABL.orCriticalProbability_pos}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, the critical probability $1-\exp(-\log(2)/n)$ lies in the
closed interval $[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential difference quotient limit]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_one_sub_exp_neg_div}
\label{FABL.tendsto_one_sub_exp_neg_div}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
As a real variable $x$ tends to $0$ through nonzero values, the quotient $(1-e^{-x})/x$
tends to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical probability scaling limit]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_nat_mul_orCriticalProbability}
\label{FABL.tendsto_nat_mul_orCriticalProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.orCriticalProbability, FABL.tendsto_one_sub_exp_neg_div}
\difficulty{5}
As $n$ tends to infinity through the natural numbers, $n\bigl(1-\exp(-\log(2)/n)\bigr)$
tends to $\log 2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical-Bias Average Complexity of OR]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_averageComplexity_or_at_critical}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p231-b004,

For each positive integer $n$, let $p_n=1-\exp(-\log(2)/n)$ and consider the OR function
on $n$ signs, equal to $+1$ when every input is $+1$ and $-1$ otherwise. Under the
product distribution in which each input is independently $-1$ with probability $p_n$,
take the infimum of the expected number of coordinate queries over all finite randomized
decision trees that compute this OR function with zero error. This infimum, divided by
$n$, tends to $1/(2\log 2)$ as $n\to\infty$.
\end{theorem}

Define a decision tree on two sign-valued inputs that first queries the first
coordinate. If its value is $1$, the tree returns $-1$; otherwise it queries the second
coordinate and returns $1$ exactly when that value is $-1$, returning $-1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

coordinate. If its value is $1$, the tree returns $-1$; otherwise it queries the first
coordinate and returns $1$ exactly when that value is $-1$, returning $-1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Recursive NAND function]
\lean{FABL.recursiveNAND}
\label{FABL.recursiveNAND}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.nandFunction, FABL.recursiveInputBlock}
For each nonnegative integer $d$, define a Boolean function on sign vectors with $2^d$
coordinates as follows: at depth zero it returns the sole input sign, and at depth $d+1$
it applies the two-input NAND function to the values obtained by recursively applying
the depth-$d$ function to the two input blocks of size $2^d$. Here NAND returns $+1$
when both inputs are $-1$, and $-1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Recursive NAND at depth zero]
\lean{FABL.recursiveNAND_zero}
\label{FABL.recursiveNAND_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.recursiveNAND}
\difficulty{1}
For every sign vector $x$ with $2^0$ coordinates, the depth-zero recursive NAND is the
value of $x$ at its sole coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Recursive NAND step]
\lean{FABL.recursiveNAND_succ}
\label{FABL.recursiveNAND_succ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.nandFunction, FABL.recursiveInputBlock, FABL.recursiveNAND}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $d$ and every sign vector $x$ with $2^{d+1}$ coordinates, the
recursive NAND of depth $d+1$ is the NAND of the two recursive NAND outputs obtained
from the two blocks of $2^d$ coordinates of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Depth of recursive NAND]
\lean{FABL.deterministicDepth_recursiveNAND_le}

tree computing the recursively defined NAND function on $2^d$ sign-valued inputs is at

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Recursive false-output cost]
\lean{FABL.recursiveNandFalseCost}

Define a real sequence $F_d$ by $F_0=1$ and $F_{d+1}=2T_d$, where $T_d$ is the

\begin{definition}[Recursive true-output cost]
\lean{FABL.recursiveNandTrueCost}

\leanok
Define a real sequence $T_d$ by $T_0=1$ and $T_{d+1}=F_d+T_d/2$, where $F_d$ is the
recursively defined false-output cost sequence.
\end{definition}

For every function $g$ from the two integer units to the reals, the sum of $g$ over
those units is $g(1)+g(-1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform mean on the three-dimensional sign cube]
\lean{FABL.expect_signCube_three_eq}
\label{FABL.expect_signCube_three_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.signCubeThreeEquiv, FABL.signCubeThreeOfSigns}
\difficulty{4}
For every function $g:\{−1,1\}^3\to\mathbb R$, its uniform mean over the
three-dimensional sign cube equals $\frac18\sum_{a,b,c\in\{−1,1\}}g(a,b,c)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average over the two signs]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformSign_eq_average}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformSign_eq_average}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.sum_sign_eq, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
For every function $g:\{\pm1\}\to\mathbb R$, its expectation under the uniform
distribution on $\{\pm1\}$ is $\frac{g(1)+g(-1)}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parameterized function on the three-dimensional sign cube]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleAt}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p243-b006}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexampleAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.signValue}
For a real parameter $t$, define a function $f_t$ on sign vectors $x=(x_0,x_1,x_2)$ by
\[
f_t(x)=\frac{t+1}{4}+\frac{t}{4}x_1+\frac{t}{4}x_2-\frac{1}{4}x_0x_1+\frac{1}{4}x_0x_2+\frac{t-1}{4}x_1x_2,
\]
where each coordinate is in $\{-1,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Parameterized decision tree]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleTree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p243-b006}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexampleTree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.Sign}
For a real parameter $t$, consider the decision tree on three sign inputs that first
queries $x_0$. If $x_0=-1$, it queries $x_1$: when $x_1=-1$ it returns $0$, and
otherwise it queries $x_2$ and returns $1$ if $x_2=-1$ and $t$ if $x_2=1$. If $x_0=1$,
it queries $x_2$: when $x_2=-1$ it returns $0$, and otherwise it queries $x_1$ and
returns $1$ if $x_1=-1$ and $t$ if $x_1=1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of the counterexample tree]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleTree_computes}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexampleTree_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.Computes, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleTree, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
For every $t\in\mathbb R$, let $f_t:\{-1,1\}^3\to\mathbb R$ be given by
$f_t(x)=\frac{t+1}{4}+\frac{t}{4}x_1+\frac{t}{4}x_2-\frac14x_0x_1+\frac14x_0x_2+\frac{t-1}{4}x_1x_2$.
The three-coordinate decision tree that first queries coordinate $0$; if $x_0=-1$,
queries coordinate $1$, returning $0$ if $x_1=-1$ and otherwise querying coordinate $2$
and returning $1$ if $x_2=-1$ or $t$ if $x_2=1$; if $x_0=1$, queries coordinate $2$,
returning $0$ if $x_2=-1$ and otherwise querying coordinate $1$ and returning $1$ if
$x_1=-1$ or $t$ if $x_1=1$, computes $f_t$ on every input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Randomized tree for a parameterized function]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p243-b006}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.ofDeterministic, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleTree, FABL.osssCounterexampleTree_computes}
For each real number $t$, there is a randomized decision tree for the function $f_t$ on
three sign inputs that is obtained by selecting the specified parameterized decision
tree with a random seed and that computes $f_t$ for every seed.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Query probability of the first coordinate]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_zero}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.structuralQueryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.ofDeterministic, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability_eq_seed_structural, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleTree, FABL.pmfExpectation_pure, FABL.signSiteFourierBasis, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
For every real parameter $t$, consider the deterministic three-coordinate decision tree
on inputs $x\in\{-1,1\}^3$ that first queries coordinate $0$; if $x_0=-1$, it queries
coordinate $1$ and, unless $x_1=-1$, then queries coordinate $2$; if $x_0=1$, it queries
coordinate $2$ and, unless $x_2=-1$, then queries coordinate $1$. When its seed is
sampled trivially and its input is sampled uniformly from the sign cube, the probability
that it queries coordinate $0$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query probability of the second coordinate]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_one}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.structuralQueryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.ofDeterministic, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability_eq_seed_structural, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleTree, FABL.pmfExpectation_pure, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformSign_eq_average, FABL.signSiteFourierBasis, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
For every real parameter $t$, consider the deterministic three-coordinate decision tree
on inputs $x\in\{-1,1\}^3$ that first queries coordinate $0$; if $x_0=-1$, it queries
coordinate $1$ and, unless $x_1=-1$, then queries coordinate $2$; if $x_0=1$, it queries
coordinate $2$ and, unless $x_2=-1$, then queries coordinate $1$. When its seed is
sampled trivially and its input is sampled uniformly from the sign cube, the probability
that it queries coordinate $1$ is $3/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query probability of the third coordinate]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_two}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_two}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.structuralQueryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.ofDeterministic, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability_eq_seed_structural, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleTree, FABL.pmfExpectation_pure, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformSign_eq_average, FABL.signSiteFourierBasis, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
For every real parameter $t$, consider the deterministic three-coordinate decision tree
on inputs $x\in\{-1,1\}^3$ that first queries coordinate $0$; if $x_0=-1$, it queries
coordinate $1$ and, unless $x_1=-1$, then queries coordinate $2$; if $x_0=1$, it queries
coordinate $2$ and, unless $x_2=-1$, then queries coordinate $1$. When its seed is
sampled trivially and its input is sampled uniformly from the sign cube, the probability
that it queries coordinate $2$ is $3/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a sign-cube polynomial]
\lean{FABL.mean_osssCounterexampleAt}
\label{FABL.mean_osssCounterexampleAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_signCube_three_eq, FABL.mean, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_sign_eq}
\difficulty{3}
For any real $t$, define a function on the three-dimensional sign cube by
\[P_t(x)=\frac{t+1}{4}+\frac{t}{4}x_1+\frac{t}{4}x_2-\frac14 x_0x_1+\frac14 x_0x_2+\frac{t-1}{4}x_1x_2.\]
Its mean over the cube is $(t+1)/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variance of a parametrized function]
\lean{FABL.variance_osssCounterexampleAt}
\label{FABL.variance_osssCounterexampleAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_signCube_three_eq, FABL.mean_osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_sign_eq, FABL.variance}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $t$, the function on the three-dimensional sign cube given by
$f_t(x)=\frac{t+1}{4}+\frac{t}{4}x_1+\frac{t}{4}x_2-\frac14x_0x_1+\frac14x_0x_2+\frac{t-1}{4}x_1x_2$
has variance $\frac{3t^2-2t+3}{16}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero coordinate derivative formula]
\lean{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_zero}
\label{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.discreteDerivative_apply, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $t$ and every point $x$ of the three-dimensional sign cube, the
discrete derivative in coordinate $0$ of the function $F_t$ at $x$ is $(-s_1+s_2)/4$,
where $s_j$ denotes the real sign value of coordinate $j$ of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First coordinate derivative formula]
\lean{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_one}
\label{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.discreteDerivative_apply, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $t$ and every point $x$ of the three-dimensional sign cube, the
discrete derivative in coordinate $1$ of the function $F_t$ at $x$ is
$(t-s_0+(t-1)s_2)/4$, where $s_j$ denotes the real sign value of coordinate $j$ of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second coordinate derivative formula]
\lean{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_two}
\label{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_two}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.discreteDerivative_apply, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $t$ and every point $x$ of the three-dimensional sign cube, the
discrete derivative in coordinate $2$ of the function $F_t$ at $x$ is
$(t+s_0+(t-1)s_1)/4$, where $s_j$ denotes the real sign value of coordinate $j$ of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence at the first coordinate]
\lean{FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_zero}
\label{FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_zero, FABL.expect_signCube_three_eq, FABL.influence, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_sign_eq}
\difficulty{3}
For each real $t$, let $f_t$ be the function on $\{−1,1\}^3$ given, for
$x=(x_0,x_1,x_2)$, by
$f_t(x)=(t+1)/4+(t/4)x_1+(t/4)x_2-(1/4)x_0x_1+(1/4)x_0x_2+((t-1)/4)x_1x_2$. Its
influence at the first coordinate, defined as the uniform average of the squared
discrete derivative in that coordinate, is $1/8$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence of the three-coordinate example]
\lean{FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_one}
\label{FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_one, FABL.expect_signCube_three_eq, FABL.influence, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_sign_eq}
\difficulty{3}
For $t\in\mathbb{R}$, define $g_t:\{-1,1\}^3\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$g_t(x)=\frac{t+1}{4}+\frac{t}{4}x_1+\frac{t}{4}x_2-\frac14x_0x_1+\frac14x_0x_2+\frac{t-1}{4}x_1x_2$.
Its influence at coordinate $1$ is $\operatorname{Inf}_1(g_t)=\frac{t^2-t+1}{8}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence at the third coordinate]
\lean{FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_two}
\label{FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_two}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.discreteDerivative_osssCounterexampleAt_two, FABL.expect_signCube_three_eq, FABL.influence, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_sign_eq}
\difficulty{3}
For each real $t$, let $f_t$ be the function on $\\{−1,1\\}^3$ given, for
$x=(x_0,x_1,x_2)$, by
$f_t(x)=(t+1)/4+(t/4)x_1+(t/4)x_2-(1/4)x_0x_1+(1/4)x_0x_2+((t-1)/4)x_1x_2$. Its
influence at the third coordinate, defined as the uniform average of the squared
discrete derivative in that coordinate, is $(t^2-t+1)/8$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[OSSS counterexample parameter]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleParameter}

The counterexample parameter is $2+\sqrt{33}/3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Counterexample function]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexample}

\label{FABL.osssCounterexample}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleParameter}
The function on sign vectors of length $3$ is the function obtained by evaluating the
parameterized counterexample function at the designated counterexample parameter.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Randomized counterexample tree]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p243-b006}

The randomized decision tree on three sign inputs is obtained by instantiating the
specified parameterized randomized tree at the designated counterexample parameter, and
it computes the corresponding counterexample function for every seed.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Query probability of the first coordinate]

\difficulty{1}

$f(x)=\frac{t+1}{4}+\frac{t}{4}x_1+\frac{t}{4}x_2-\frac14x_0x_1+\frac14x_0x_2+\frac{t-1}{4}x_1x_2$,
where $t=2+\frac{\sqrt{33}}{3}$. Consider the decision tree that first queries
coordinate $0$; if $x_0=-1$, it queries coordinate $1$ and, unless $x_1=-1$, then

\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.productInfluence_osssCounterexample_zero}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted influence sum]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexample_weightedInfluenceSum}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexample_weightedInfluenceSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssCounterexample, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTree, FABL.osssCounterexample_queryProbability_one, FABL.osssCounterexample_queryProbability_two, FABL.osssCounterexample_queryProbability_zero, FABL.productInfluence, FABL.productInfluence_osssCounterexample_one, FABL.productInfluence_osssCounterexample_two, FABL.productInfluence_osssCounterexample_zero, FABL.uniformPMF}

\begin{theorem}[Variance exceeds the weighted influence sum]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexample_violates_real_valued_extension}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p243-b006}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexample_violates_real_valued_extension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssCounterexample, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTree, FABL.osssCounterexample_weightedInfluenceSum, FABL.productInfluence, FABL.productVariance, FABL.productVariance_osssCounterexample, FABL.uniformPMF}

  {FABL.productInfluence_osssCounterexample_two}

\proofstep
  {FABL.osssCounterexample_weightedInfluenceSum}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p232-b006}
Let $f$ be the specified real-valued function on the three-dimensional cube of signs,
and let $T$ be its specified zero-error randomized decision tree. Under the uniform
distribution on the sign cube, the sum over coordinates of the probability that $T$
queries that coordinate, multiplied by the coordinate influence of $f$, is strictly less
than the variance of $f$. Here coordinate influence is the expected square of the
difference between $f$ and its average over that coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact variance-to-influence ratio]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexample_exact_ratio}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexample_exact_ratio}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssCounterexample, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTree, FABL.osssCounterexample_weightedInfluenceSum, FABL.productInfluence, FABL.productVariance, FABL.productVariance_osssCounterexample, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^3\to\mathbb R$ be defined by
$f(x)=\frac{t+1}{4}+\frac{t}{4}x_1+\frac{t}{4}x_2-\frac14x_0x_1+\frac14x_0x_2+\frac{t-1}{4}x_1x_2$,
where $t=2+\frac{\sqrt{33}}{3}$. Equip the sign cube with the uniform product
probability distribution, and let $T$ be the decision tree that first queries coordinate
$0$; if $x_0=-1$, it queries coordinate $1$ and, unless $x_1=-1$, then queries
coordinate $2$; if $x_0=1$, it queries coordinate $2$ and, unless $x_2=-1$, then queries
coordinate $1$. Then the variance of $f$ divided by the sum, over the three coordinates
$i$, of the probability that $T$ queries $i$ times the influence of coordinate $i$ on
$f$ is $\frac{42+2\sqrt{33}}{51}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Book counterexample parameter]
\lean{FABL.osssBookCounterexampleParameter}
\label{FABL.osssBookCounterexampleParameter}
\leanok
The counterexample parameter is the real number $2+\sqrt{3}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Book counterexample function]
\lean{FABL.osssBookCounterexample}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p243-b006}
\label{FABL.osssBookCounterexample}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.osssBookCounterexampleParameter, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt}
The book counterexample is the function on sign vectors of length $3$ obtained by
evaluating the parameterized counterexample function at the designated
book-counterexample parameter.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Randomized tree for the counterexample]
\lean{FABL.osssBookCounterexampleTree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p243-b006}
\label{FABL.osssBookCounterexampleTree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssBookCounterexample, FABL.osssBookCounterexampleParameter, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt}
A randomized decision tree on three sign-valued coordinates with real-valued output is
defined to compute the function $f\colon\{−1,1\}^3\to\bbr$ given by
\[
f(x)=\frac{t+1}{4}+\frac{t}{4}x_1+\frac{t}{4}x_2-\frac14x_0x_1+\frac14x_0x_2+\frac{t-1}{4}x_1x_2,
\qquad t=2+\sqrt3.
\]
The tree has a finite, nonempty seed space with a probability distribution, and every
seed selects a deterministic decision tree that computes $f$ on every input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Variance of the first counterexample function]
\lean{FABL.productVariance_osssBookCounterexample}
\label{FABL.productVariance_osssBookCounterexample}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.osssBookCounterexample, FABL.osssBookCounterexampleParameter, FABL.productVariance, FABL.productVariance_uniformSign, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.variance_osssCounterexampleAt}
\difficulty{3}
On the three-dimensional sign cube, let the function be the one defined by the parameter
$t=2+\sqrt{3}$ in the displayed polynomial in the three sign coordinates. Its variance
under the uniform distribution on the cube is $(20+10\sqrt{3})/16$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Counterexample weighted influence sum]
\lean{FABL.osssBookCounterexample_weightedInfluenceSum}
\label{FABL.osssBookCounterexample_weightedInfluenceSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.Sign, FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_one, FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_two, FABL.influence_osssCounterexampleAt_zero, FABL.osssBookCounterexample, FABL.osssBookCounterexampleParameter, FABL.osssBookCounterexampleTree, FABL.osssCounterexampleAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_one, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_two, FABL.osssCounterexampleRandomizedTreeAt_queryProbability_zero, FABL.productInfluence, FABL.productInfluence_uniformSign_eq_influence, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
For the specified function $F$ on the three-dimensional sign cube and its specified
randomized decision tree $T$, let $\\operatorname{Inf}_i(F)$ be the squared $L^2$ norm
of the coordinate-$i$ product Laplacian, and let $q_i$ be the probability that $T$
queries coordinate $i$ on a uniformly random input. Then $\\sum_{i=0}^2
q_i\\operatorname{Inf}_i(F)=(20+9\\sqrt3)/16$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact counterexample variance ratio]
\lean{FABL.osssBookCounterexample_exact_ratio}
\label{FABL.osssBookCounterexample_exact_ratio}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.Sign, FABL.osssBookCounterexample, FABL.osssBookCounterexampleTree, FABL.osssBookCounterexample_weightedInfluenceSum, FABL.productInfluence, FABL.productVariance, FABL.productVariance_osssBookCounterexample, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
For the specified function $F$ on the three-dimensional sign cube and its specified
randomized decision tree $T$, let $\\operatorname{Var}(F)$ be the variance under the
uniform sign distribution, let $\\operatorname{Inf}_i(F)$ be the squared $L^2$ norm of
the coordinate-$i$ product Laplacian, and let $q_i$ be the probability that $T$ queries
coordinate $i$ on a uniformly random input. Then $\\operatorname{Var}(F)/(\\sum_{i=0}^2
q_i\\operatorname{Inf}_i(F))=(130+20\\sqrt3)/157$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict comparison of counterexample ratios]
\lean{FABL.osssCounterexample_ratio_strictly_larger_than_book}
\label{FABL.osssCounterexample_ratio_strictly_larger_than_book}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
The ratio $(130+20\sqrt{3})/157$ is strictly less than $(42+2\sqrt{33})/51$.
\end{theorem}
